claims.text: Imin and Iminyë wandered with the two other Fathers and their spouses, Tata and Tatië, Enel and Enelyë, until they found a group of 12 sleeping Elves which he took with him. That clan was named after him Minyar, the "Firsts".
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The War of the Jewels, "Part Four. Quendi and Eldar"

claims.text: The clan was later named Vanyar. He also founded the House of Imin.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The War of the Jewels, "Part Four. Quendi and Eldar", pp. 380-1; J.R.R. Tolkien, Carl F. Hostetter (ed.), "Part One. Time and Ageing: XIII. Key Dates", The Nature of Middle-earth, HarperCollins, 2021, pp. 95-7

claims.text: At the Debate of the Quendi, Imin disagreed with the departure from Cuiviénen and, claiming the title of "Father of All Quendi" (Ilquendatar), asserted that he had the right of decision.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Carl F. Hostetter (ed.), "Part One. Time and Ageing: XIII. Key Dates", The Nature of Middle-earth, HarperCollins, 2021
